finding.claim: Webhook delivery ignores subscription ownership and CA scope. Any operator who can create a webhook subscription receives lifecycle events for every tenant's hosts: host names, host/network/CA IDs, and cert fingerprints.
finding.source: Authenticated non-admin operator (bearer API key) calls POST /api/v1/webhook-subscriptions with a public URL and no events filter (or events: [host.enrolled, cert.expiring, ...]). Attacker is a low-privilege tenant, not an admin.
finding.sink: Dispatcher.dispatch -> deliver() POSTs JSON event payloads containing other tenants' host_name, host_id, network_id, ca_id, fingerprint to the attacker URL.

trace.note: Subscription create/list routes are mounted in the bearerAuth group, with no admin requirement.
handleCreateWebhookSubscription: any authenticated operator may create a subscription; OwnerOperatorID is set to the caller (line 89).
Only allow_private is admin-gated; no check on which events or CAs the subscription may receive.
owner_operator_id is stored on every subscription.
Lifecycle events emitted with hostEventData for any host, regardless of owner: host.deleted, host.blocked (370), host.unblocked (408), cert.rotated with fingerprint (519).
hostEventData carries host_id, host_name, network_id, ca_id.
host.enrolled emitted for any enrolling host, including fingerprint.
cert.expiring emitted for alerts that carry host_name, network_id, ca_id, fingerprint, not_after; alerts are not owner-filtered.
Emit queues every event globally. The comment at 175-176 says per-target filtering happens at delivery.
targets() collects managed subscriptions through source.TargetsFor for the event type.
ListActiveWebhookSubscriptions loads every active subscription in the deployment.
Only filter is wantsEvent(event type). Empty events list matches every event (lines 75-77). No owner, CA, or network check exists.
Contrast: the UI SSE stream drops events whose NetworkID is not owned by the operator. The webhook path has no equivalent.

finding.guards_checked: bearerAuth (api/middleware.go:35-70) authenticates the caller but does not scope events. Admin gate applies only to allow_private (webhooks.go:73,127). ValidateWebhookURL (config/server.go:188) blocks private targets but is orthogonal to tenancy. Owner scoping exists only on list/get/update/delete (webhooks.go:38-47, 183-199), not on delivery. Existing tests (webhook/fanout_test.go:118-134) assert only event-type filtering. Impact: cross-tenant metadata disclosure of other tenants' host names, IDs, and cert fingerprints, plus lifecycle timing for their hosts. Precondition: an operator with an API key, which only an admin can mint (api/operators.go:141), so this is an authenticated tenant-boundary break, not an unauthenticated one.

finding.claim: Overlay IP uniqueness compares raw submitted strings, not parsed addresses. Two hosts in the same network can hold the same IPv6 address written in different textual forms (for example fd00::1 and FD00:0::1), so duplicate overlay IPs are accepted at both the API and web layers.
finding.source: Authenticated operator who owns the network's CA (non-admin tenant) sends nebula_ips in POST /api/v1/hosts, PATCH /api/v1/hosts/{id}, or the web host create/edit forms.
finding.sink: Two host rows whose certificates and config carry the same overlay address. The store UNIQUE(network_id, address) index is also on the raw string.

trace.note: handleCreateHost calls validateHostIPs with the raw req.NebulaIPs.
netip.ParseAddr validates syntax only; the original string is kept.
seenIPs is keyed by the raw ip string, so the within-request duplicate check is spelling-sensitive.
Cross-host check compares the stored raw string (seenIPs[hIP]). A differently spelled existing address is not caught.
Host.NebulaIPs = req.NebulaIPs stores the raw spelling.
setHostAddresses inserts addr raw. ON CONFLICT(network_id, address) compares strings, so the DB guard is spelling-sensitive too.
Web path has the same bug: hostIP == ip raw comparison (used by handlers.go:852 create and handlers.go:1127 edit).

finding.guards_checked: ParseAddr syntax check; CIDR containment (validate_ip.go:108-123); IPv4 network/broadcast rejection (126-128); exact-string duplicate detection within one request (131-134); cross-host exact-string check (146-148); store UNIQUE(network_id, address) (sqlite.go:796). Only the exact-string case is caught. The models.ValidateHostIPs canonicalizing check (models/validate_ip.go:131) runs only within a single list and is not used on the cross-host path. Impact is limited to the network owner's own mesh (no cross-tenant reach), so severity is low: overlay address collision inside one tenant's network, causing ambiguous routing and cert identity.
